title: Vinkle F1 Corn (Vinkle): Characteristics
metaDescription: Vinkle F1 corn is a glutinous hybrid corn variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Vinkle F1 corn is a glutinous hybrid corn variety, also sold or known as Vinkle or Waxy Bicolor Vinkle F1. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Ramgo Seeds (Ramgo International).

heroImage.alt: A cornfield on a hillside in Pilar, Capiz, its leaves drying close to harvest, the kind of farm where Vinkle F1 corn is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Vinkle or Waxy Bicolor Vinkle F1, this is the same corn. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [corn variety finder](/crop-varieties/corn), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Pagtatanim ng mais, step by step](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-mais).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: about 68 days after sowing (60 to 70 days on the garden packet). No trial on record checks this figure yet, so treat it as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit corn fields most often: [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [banded leaf and sheath blight](/diseases/banded-leaf-and-sheath-blight), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Corn ear rot](/diseases/corn-ear-rot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** About 68 days after sowing (60 to 70 days on the garden packet).
Big ears with good tip fill and closed husk tips.
Pearl white and dark purple kernels with a sticky, chewy bite.
A high share of class A ears.
Resists the main diseases of waxy corn, its seller says.

blocks.text: These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual corn on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Vinkle F1 corn

Start with the color your buyer pays for: yellow corn goes to feed mills, while white and glutinous corn go to the table. Next, pick between a hybrid, which yields more but needs new seed every season, and an open pollinated variety, whose seed you can save. Then match the island group in its recommendation, because trials in Luzon and Mindanao give different winners. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for corn](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Vinkle the same as Vinkle F1?
items.a: Yes. Vinkle is another name for Vinkle F1. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Vinkle F1?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
